newsitem.title: GERMANY: Frankfurt shares reel from high as dollar drops.
newsitem.headline: Frankfurt shares reel from high as dollar drops.

text.p: German shares, after volatile trading on Thursday, were expected to head into Friday depending heavily on overnight results of Wall Street and dollar trading, dealers said.
The IBIS DAX stood at 2,892.69 by 1515 GMT, up 11.80 but more than 20 points below the high of 2,916.16 reached earlier.
The fall from the record high was prompted by a drop in German bonds and then a fall in the dollar.
"When they went down, they took stocks with them," one Frankfurt trader said. "No idea about tomorrow, but it's going to depend on the Dow and the dollar."
March Bunds, which had fueled the stock rally by climbing 30 basis points earlier, slumped in the afternoon to 100.97, down 47 points by 1525 GMT.
Earlier, the dollar fed the DAX rally, holding steady at 1.56 marks. When the dollar dropped to 1.5540 by 1525 GMT, shares eased back, especially export-driven shares.
Car maker BMW AG, which traded down 19.3 at 1,050 marks by 1430 GMT, had been as high as 1,089.
Mannesmann AG, which had soared on rumour of a telecommunicaitons alliance with utility Veba AG, also pared back gains by 1500 GMT to stand at 673 marks, up 4.20.
The Dow Jones index climbed 21.62 to 6,44.56 within an hour, laying a foundation for optimism in Frankfurt on Friday.
The DAX climb to record highs early on Thursday after a late surge by the Dow the day before, when the U.S. index narrowed its loss to 19 points after falling as much as 79.

German unemployment and the Bundesbank gave less definitive signals for Friday's direction. Seasonally adjsusted unemployment in November rose 50,000 to a record 4.1 million, a sign the economy wasn't gaining momentum.
But the Bundesbank kept key interest rates unchanged, an announcement that pushed Bunds downward.
